# Set Up an Alexa+ Routine That Changes by Day of the Week

> **In short:** Alexa+ routines can branch by time and day, so one wake-up routine can run different steps on weekdays (news, traffic, coffee) versus weekends (sleep-in music, no alarm). Conditional logic in Alexa+ is limited compared to a full smart-home hub — but for simple day-of-week splits, it works well.

If you've already set up a basic Alexa+ routine and want it to behave differently on Saturday morning than on Monday morning, this guide walks you through the conditional steps. You'll build one routine with two branches, test both, and know what Alexa+ can and can't do when days collide.

## Before you start
- An **Alexa+ enabled Echo device** (or the Alexa+ app on your phone) with the latest firmware
- The **Alexa app** signed in to the same Amazon account as your Echo
- A name picked out for your routine (something you'll remember saying, like "Start my morning")
- About **15 minutes** the first time, once you know the layout it's closer to 5

## Step 1 — Open the Routines section
In the Alexa app, tap the **More** tab in the bottom-right corner (it looks like three horizontal lines or dots, depending on your device). From the menu that opens, choose **Routines**. You'll land on a list of any routines you've made before, with a big **+** button or **Create Routine** button at the top of the screen. Tap it.

If you can't find Routines under **More**, use the search bar at the top of the app and type "Routines." The app may also have moved this under **Settings → Routines** on older versions.

💬 Example: routine name — `Start my morning`

You'll know it worked when the screen shows a fresh routine form with fields for a routine name, a trigger ("When this happens"), and actions ("Add action").

## Step 2 — Set the voice trigger and the time window
In the **When this happens** box, tap **Enter routine name** and type a short phrase Alexa will listen for, such as "start my morning." Then tap **At a specific time** and pick your wake-up hour and minute. Leave the days-of-week selector at its default for now — we'll add the day branching in the next step.

If your app shows a **Voice** option instead of typing the phrase, tap the microphone icon and say the trigger out loud; the app will transcribe it for confirmation.

💬 Example: trigger phrase — *"Alexa, start my morning"* at **6:30 AM**

You'll know it worked when the routine form shows your phrase and time at the top, and the days-of-week row says "Every day" (or similar) with little check marks.

## Step 3 — Restrict the first action group to weekdays
Tap **Add action** and pick the first action you want on weekdays — for most people that's something like **Music → Play news flash** or **Smart Home → Turn on kitchen lights**. After you select the action, the app will usually ask "When?" — choose **Weekday mornings** or pick each weekday manually (Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri). This is the **conditional logic** part: the action is now tied to specific days, not just to the time.

If your version of the app does not show a day selector for individual actions, look for a **Conditions** section at the bottom of the routine form — it's the same idea, just worded differently.

💬 Example: action — **News → Flash Briefing**, restricted to **Mon–Fri only**

You'll know it worked when you can see the action listed with a small "Weekday" tag or a checkmark beside Mon through Fri.

## Step 4 — Add the weekend-only branch
Tap **Add action** again and pick a different action — the one you only want on Saturday and Sunday. Common picks: a gentle sleep-in playlist, a longer snooze-style lighting fade, or skipping the news flash entirely. Again, the app should ask which days this runs. Choose **Weekend mornings**, or check **Sat** and **Sun** manually.

If the app doesn't separate the two branches automatically, that's fine — both actions will sit in the same list, each with its own day filter. Alexa+ will run only the ones whose day matches today.

💬 Example: action — **Music → Play "Sleepy Sunday" playlist**, restricted to **Sat–Sun only**

You'll know it worked when the routine list shows two actions, each tagged with different days, and no action is set to run on all seven days.

## Step 5 — Add shared actions that run every day
Some actions probably belong on **both** branches — the coffee maker turning on, a weather check, a "good morning" announcement. Add those next, and this time, when the app asks which days, choose **Every day** (or check Mon through Sun). These actions will run regardless of whether it's a weekday or weekend.

If an action doesn't give you a day option, set it to **Every day** by default and just leave it — the app usually only asks the first time or two.

💬 Example: shared action — **Smart Home → Turn on "Coffee Maker" plug**, set to **Every day**

You'll know it worked when scrolling the routine shows three groups: weekday-only, weekend-only, and every-day actions, each clearly labeled.

## Step 6 — Test both branches without waiting for the clock
Save the routine, then go back into it and tap **Test routine** (sometimes labeled **Try it now** or **Run routine**). Run it once with your phone's date set to a weekday in the Alexa app's settings, and once with it set to a weekend, if the app lets you — this confirms each branch fires. If the app doesn't offer date simulation, just manually disable and re-enable the weekday actions to test the weekend ones, or set your phone's system clock briefly forward (and remember to set it back).

If the test plays both branches at once, you almost certainly left one action's day filter on **Every day** — go back and tighten it to Mon–Fri or Sat–Sun only.

💬 Example: in the Alexa app, **Settings → Device Settings → Clock & Time Format → Set Time** — temporarily move the clock to 6:30 AM on a Saturday to trigger the weekend branch.

You'll know it worked when you see the weekday run flash news and skip your sleep-in playlist, and the weekend run starts the playlist instead.

## Step 7 — Save and document your setup
Tap **Save** or **Create** at the top-right of the screen. Alexa+ will confirm with a "Routine saved" banner. Take a screenshot of the final action list and save it in a notes app — six months from now, when the routine misbehaves, you'll want to remember which day filter you set on which action. Routine logic in Alexa+ is not visible from the Echo itself, so the phone screenshot is your only reference.

If the routine does nothing when triggered, the most common cause is the trigger phrase being slightly different from what Alexa heard — go back to Step 2 and double-check the exact spelling.

💬 Example: screenshot the action list, then in your notes app write: *"Routine 'Start my morning' — News flash (Mon–Fri), Sleepy Sunday playlist (Sat–Sun), Coffee Maker (Every day)."*

You'll know it worked when the next real weekday morning, your Echo plays the news at 6:30 AM, and the following Saturday, it skips the news and starts your weekend playlist instead.

## Common mistakes
- **Setting the trigger time but forgetting to restrict the actions.** The routine fires every day, so weekday actions also run on Saturday. Fix: go into each action and set its day filter to Mon–Fri or Sat–Sun — never leave them all on "Every day" unless you mean it.
- **Naming the routine something Alexa mishears.** "Start my mourning" is a common autocorrect trap. Fix: use the app's **Test routine** button and watch what the screen logs — if the phrase doesn't match what you said, edit it.
- **Adding two competing music actions for the same day.** Alexa+ can play only one stream at a time, so if both a news flash and a playlist are tagged Mon–Fri, one will cut the other off mid-sentence. Fix: stagger them with a **Wait** action (usually under the ⋯ menu in the action picker) — three minutes between news and playlist is enough.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** you stop saying "Alexa, good morning" on weekdays and "Alexa, good morning weekend" on Saturdays — one phrase, two experiences, zero thinking. The routine also gently handles the case where you forget which day it is, because Alexa+ always does.
- **For your business or work:** if you run a small home-based business, the same day-of-week pattern works for opening routines — turn on the office printer and play focus music on weekdays, leave them off on weekends. The same conditional logic that splits your morning can split your workday.
- **If you want to go further:** Alexa+ routines can also branch on **device**, **location** (home/away), and **alarm state** — so you could have one routine that says "good morning" if you're home, "see you later" if you've already left, and a different message entirely if Alexa+ thinks you just woke from a nap. Layer these one at a time and test each before adding the next.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, go to **More → Routines → Create Routine**, and set up just the trigger phrase plus **one** weekday action (your favorite news flash). Save it, say the phrase out loud, and confirm the action runs. You've now built the smallest version of a conditional routine — the weekend branch is one tap away whenever you're ready.
